detailed_section_hierarchy.full_explanation: Assuming equally likely outcomes: P(E) = n(E) / n(S). For any event E, 0 <= P(E) <= 1.

margin_boxes_and_in_text_notes.full_content: P(E) = Number of outcomes favorable to E / Total number of possible outcomes

detailed_section_hierarchy.full_explanation: Event 'not E' is Ē. P(E) + P(Ē) = 1. Impossible event: P = 0. Sure/Certain event: P = 1.

level_2_short_answer_questions_2_to_3_ma.question: A die is thrown once. Find probability of getting a prime number.
level_2_short_answer_questions_2_to_3_ma.model_answer: Total outcomes S = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} => n(S) = 6. Prime numbers = {2, 3, 5} => n(E) = 3. P(Prime) = 3/6 = 1/2.

level_3_long_answer_and_reasoning_5_mark.question: Two dice are thrown at same time. Find probability that sum of numbers is: (i) 8, (ii) 13, (iii) less than or equal to 12.
level_3_long_answer_and_reasoning_5_mark.model_answer: n(S) = 36. (i) Favorable for sum 8: {(2,6),(3,5),(4,4),(5,3),(6,2)} => 5/36. (ii) Favorable for sum 13: 0 => P=0. (iii) Favorable for sum <= 12: all 36 outcomes => 36/36 = 1.

level_4_competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: A box contains 90 discs numbered 1 to 90. One disc drawn at random.

questions_and_answers.question: Find probability that it bears a two-digit number.
questions_and_answers.answer: Two-digit numbers: 10 to 90 => total 81 discs. P = 81/90 = 9/10.
